A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material. The framework's rename from TIGER to TiGeSR does not impede comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original Real-CE and UZ-ST evaluations, component ablations, alignment experiments, and efficiency measurements in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark comparisons and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The two-stage architecture, two-phase text-restoration training, glyph-conditioned image enhancement, losses, and inference procedures remain unchanged. TiGeSR is a rename; Figure 2's additional labels explain the existing pipeline.

E1.justification: Both use the same LSDIR-derived synthetic training data, Real-CE and UZ-ST benchmarks, zoom scenarios, and supplementary Japanese/Korean qualitative examples. No dataset, task, or language coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The comparator sets remain identical in the benchmark, ablation, alignment, and efficiency experiments. This includes the twelve benchmark baselines in Tables 2–3 and the RealSR/SIFT alignment comparisons in Table 8.

E3.justification: The splits, sample counts, preprocessing, metrics, training budgets, and model settings are retained. Both evaluate Real-CE at ×4 and UZ-ST across the same three zoom levels.

E4.justification: The training-data, OCR-input, and mask-guidance ablations remain unchanged, as do the supplementary OCR-randomness, alignment, and efficiency analyses. No new robustness test or case study appears.

E5.justification: Both retain the same point-estimate reporting without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The OCR-randomness experiments are unchanged input-perturbation analyses.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative outputs match throughout the main text and supplement. For example, Table 2 retains the proposed method's OCR-A scores of 67.3% on Real-CE and 43.0% on UZ-ST; Table 11's detailed results also match.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), including the training losses, latent update, and OCR-A definition, remain mathematically equivalent. Differences in equation rendering and extraction do not change the mathematics; no new assumptions or proofs appear.

C1.justification: Both claim a text-first two-stage framework, the UZ-ST benchmark, and superior restoration performance. Replacing 'extreme zoom' with explicit maximum-zoom wording preserves the ×14.29 scope already stated in v2.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning glyph decoupling, OCR dependence, baseline failures, and alignment remain unchanged. The supplementary inference-speed tradeoff and ethical qualifications are also retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds a first-page project-page hyperlink. Implementation details remain unchanged, and Section 7 still promises future code and dataset release, so the PDFs establish added access information rather than verified resource availability.

R1.justification: The same 59 numbered references and substantive related-work positioning are retained. Reference reflow and changed citation backreferences do not add or remove cited research.

P1.justification: v3 renames TIGER to TiGeSR, makes localized wording corrections, updates author and affiliation information, and adds funding acknowledgments. The main narrative and supplementary section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 adds explicit denoising-step, conditioning, and output labels. Other figures and tables receive renamed labels and small placement adjustments. Added front matter reflows the abstract and references; all existing displays are retained.

improvement.justification: Clearer Figure 2 annotations and the new project-page link modestly improve explanation and resource discoverability. The scientific evidence is unchanged, and the abstract now awkwardly continues into the second column, limiting the overall gain.
